subject: physical-education
unitTitle: Health-Related Fitness and Personal Activity Planning
title: Guided practice A: building cardiorespiratory endurance enjoyably
essentialQuestion: How do I build an activity plan that fits my body and my life?
materials: unit equipment listed in the guardian safety review
movementCues: Splitting activity across the day still counts.
commonErrorToWatchFor: Starting too hard and stopping within a week. Fix: begin below what feels possible and build slowly.
keyPoints: Splitting activity across the day still counts.
privacySafeScenario: Build a two-week personal activity plan based on enjoyment, access, safety, and recovery. No weight, body measurement, calorie, timing, or fitness-test target may appear in it.
studentTask: The learner practises building cardiorespiratory endurance enjoyably at a self-selected challenge level, using the adapted alternative whenever it fits better, and names the cue that helped.
knowledgeCheck: The learner names one cue that helped with building cardiorespiratory endurance enjoyably and one adjustment for next time, by demonstrating, describing, drawing, or writing.
completionCriteria: The learner takes part in the task about building cardiorespiratory endurance enjoyably at a self-selected challenge level.
The learner uses or names the movement cues for building cardiorespiratory endurance enjoyably.
The learner identifies one adjustment or next step. No score, time, count, or measurement is required.
adaptationChoices: Every fitness activity has a lower-impact, seated, and shorter-duration version. Intensity is chosen by the learner using their own sense of effort. No learner is timed against another, ranked, or measured; there is no fitness test, no score, and no body measurement.
extensionChallenge: Apply building cardiorespiratory endurance enjoyably under one new condition of the learner choosing — different equipment, space, speed, or partner — and describe what changed.
accessibilitySupports: Provide readable text plus optional audio or read-aloud support; no voice feature is required.
Chunk directions into one action at a time and show or describe a model before practice.
Allow demonstrated, described, drawn, spoken, signed, or written evidence; the response mode is never the standard being assessed.
Offer reduced-repetition, extended-time, hidden-timer, rest-break, and low-stimulation options.
Use captions, alt text, high-contrast print, keyboard access, and text-only fallbacks for any media.
Preserve the movement target while adjusting equipment, distance, speed, force, duration, or support.

optionalReflection.prompt: Invite the learner to enjoy one safe, optional activity that practises building cardiorespiratory endurance enjoyably. No purchase, account creation, recording, measurement, or public performance is required.

neverRequires: This task never requires body weight, height, BMI, or body-fat percentage.
This task never requires calorie counting or a diet or weight-loss goal.
This task never requires disclosing private medical history, a diagnosis, or sexual history.
This task never requires a photograph, video, or voice recording of the learner as proof.
This task never requires a public performance or an audience.
